- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 3% max after spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a peak, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags true trend by 2–4 days — if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.33), model tends to misalign horizon — use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast.
